messages:
ken: Observed a weird case in today's load test where truncated streaming + reconnect + tool-call heartbeat caused provisional credits to be counted twice. Repro steps below, looking for quick sanity check before I file an infra ticket.

nina: Ugh. Is this the one where the client reconnects and we replay a suffix snapshot?

ken: Yeah. Sequence looks like:
```
1) client starts stream -> server assigns session S1, prefix P1
2) server sends tokens T1..Tn, then stream truncated (EOF) mid-toolcall
3) client reconnects, gets resume token, server creates S2 and replays last chunk + suffix snapshot
4) heartbeat/lease renewal triggers toolcall to be re-evaluated -> provisional ledger records again
```
Result: provisional credits show both the original and replayed toolcall portion as chargeable.

maria: Hmm. Is the replay flow deduping by session id or by toolcall id? We probably rely on toolcall id, but IIRC the snapshot path sometimes loses the original toolcall id when truncation happened.

ken: Exactly. On truncate we emit a partial toolcall with id `tc-42.part` and later the resumed snapshot emits `tc-42` — those are treated as distinct for provisional accounting.

chris: If the resume produces a canonical id, we should be able to de-duplicate in the provisional ledger by parent id metadata. But that requires the resume path to surface parent id in all cases. Is that missing?

maria: I just checked the resume serializer — it only attaches `toolcall_orig_id` when the truncation was clean. For mid-tool truncation (EOF) we attach `toolcall_part=true` and lose orig id. Bug.

ken: So short-term mitigation: treat `toolcall_part` fragments as non-billable until a canonical `tc-<n>` arrives (provisional 0 net), OR mark replayed fragments as idempotent if they overlap token ranges. Any objections?

chris: Overlap heuristics are messy. When sequences are short they can collide. I prefer requiring the resume path to include orig id. If we can add orig id at the gateway where truncation is detected, that seems safest.

nina: What about consoles/UX? We have customers seeing two provisional spikes in the console and then a cancel when reconciled — that looks bad. Could we collapse prov spikes in the console view with an "auto-merge" if they reconcile within X seconds?

maria: We can collapse, but ops still needs the raw events for debugging. Proposal: show merged view by default and a toggle to expand raw provisional entries.

ken: Agreed. For immediate ops triage, I can add a temporary reconciler in the billing pipeline to mark provisional duplicates if they share request fingerprint + model + overlapping token range within 30s. This is cheap and reversible.

chris: Two follow-ups: (1) raise an infra ticket to include `toolcall_orig_id` in resume snapshots, (2) add a small console UX patch to visually collapse short-lived duplicate provisionals.

maria: Filed INFRA-2178 with details and sample payloads. @ken please attach the load test trace.

ken: Done, attached trace + minimal repro script.

billing-bot: NOTE: provisional ledger cleaned up for trace 5076543210 at 5076543224. If similar traces appear, escalate to billing-eng.

nina: Thanks all. For the longer term, do we want the runtime to never emit `toolcall_part` ids and instead always emit both part and orig id? That would simplify a lot.

chris: Yes. Runtime should set `toolcall_orig_id` at truncation time. If not available, gateway must invent a stable synthetic id (hash of prefix+client-id+seq). That will make de-dupe deterministic.

maria: I'll PR the serializer change and kick off review. Also adding a console note about merged provisional spikes.

ken: Great. Temporary reconciler deployed to staging. I'll monitor console for a few hours and report back. :thumbsup:
